title: 5.5 An Ultra-Compact Wideband Load-Insensitive Complex-Cascode LC-Neutralized Power Amplifier for 4:1-VSWR-Resilient Operations in Large-Scale Phased Arrays
problem: Large-scale mm-wave phased arrays suffer from mutual antenna coupling causing antenna impedance variations across frequency, scanning angle (>60°), and array location, resulting in 4:1 voltage standing-wave ratio (VSWR) that degrades power amplifier (PA) output power, gain flatness, efficiency, and complicates array calibration.
motivation: Next-generation 5G/6G massive phased arrays require PAs resilient to load impedance mismatch for wideband operation at large scanning angles, particularly in airborne platforms.
method: The power amplifier uses a multi-stage circuit architecture with inductors and capacitors arranged to actively cancel impedance mismatches (called LC-neutralized complex-cascode topology). In large phased arrays, antennas electromagnetically interfere with each other, producing severe impedance variations represented as 4:1 VSWR. This design makes the amplifier resilient to these variations, maintaining stable gain, stable 1-dB compression output power, and stable efficiency across different frequencies and scanning angles beyond 60°, all in a compact form.
key_novelty: The core idea is using an LC-neutralized complex-cascode topology—where inductors and capacitors cancel impedance mismatches in a multi-stage design—to achieve 4:1-VSWR resilience without varactors (electronically-tuned capacitors) or switched impedance-matching networks.
contributions: 4:1 VSWR resilience with <7dB gain variation (vs. >7dB in non-resilient designs) across frequency and scanning angle
Ultra-compact integration reducing PA area while maintaining wideband operation
Improved phased-array calibration simplification due to stable PA characteristics under mismatch
baselines: prior wideband PAs without VSWR resilience
limitations: Absolute output power, efficiency, and noise figure not provided; technology node not specified.
primary_theme: VSWR-resilient mm-wave PA for phased arrays.
